Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:11:1.hebrew: אבות דמתני' - הזיק דבידים, ד' שומרין הזיק דממילא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:11:1.english: The primary categories of our mishna - [Are] damage [done] directly, [and the] four bailees [are] damage [that occurs] on its own.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:12:1.english: Double payment - [As it is written:] "If the theft is found in his hand" (Exodus 22:3).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:12:2.english: Fourfold and fivefold payment - In [the case of one who] slaughters and sells.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:12:3.hebrew: וגנב - שמשלם ע"פ עצמו, ואינו משלם כפל אלא קרן בלבד, וכגון שהודה מעצמו, דמודה בקנס פטור, כדאמרינן: אשר ירשיעון אלהים ישלם שנים, והיינו קנס, ואמרינן בפ' מרובה (לקמן בבא קמא דף סד:): פרט למרשיע את עצמו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:12:3.english: And a thief - [This refers to a thief] who pays based on his own admission, and does not pay double, but rather the principal alone; such as where he confessed of his own accord, for one who admits to a penalty is exempt [from the penalty], as we say: "Whom the judges condemn, he shall pay double" [Exodus 22:8] — and that is a penalty — and we say in the chapter [entitled] "Merubah" (below, Bava Kamma 64b): "[This] excludes one who condemns himself."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:12:4.hebrew: וגזלן - נמי אב הוא, דכתיב: והשיב את הגזלה אשר גזל (ויקרא ה׳:כ״ג):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:12:4.english: And a robber - Is also a primary category, as it is written: "And he shall return that which he took by robbery" (Leviticus 5:23).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:1.hebrew: אונס ומפתה - כתיבי: חמשים כסף כתיב באונס (דברים כ״ב:כ״ט), ובמפתה כתיב (שמות כ״ב:ט״ז): כסף ישקל כמוהר הבתולות, כמוהר בתולים של אונס, דהיינו חמשים כסף:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:1.english: The rapist and the seducer - [They are] written [in Scripture]: "Fifty [shekels of] silver" is written regarding the rapist (Deuteronomy 22:29), and regarding the seducer it is written (Exodus 22:16): "He shall weigh silver according to the bride-price of virgins" — like the virginity bride-price of the rapist, which is fifty [shekels of] silver.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:2.english: One who defames - It is written: "And they shall fine him one hundred [shekels of] silver" (Deuteronomy 22:19).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:3.english: One who defiles - [That is, he defiles] terumah.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:4.english: One who mixes - [That is, he mixes] terumah into non-sacred produce.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:5.hebrew: ומנסך - יין לע"ז, ובמס' גיטין (דף נב:) מפרש אמאי לא קם ליה בדרבה מיניה. מטמא, מדמע, ומנסך לא כתיבי בהדיא, ואפ"ה הוו אבות, שבכלל נזק הן, ונזק ממון כתיב בתורה (ויקרא כ״ד:י״ח): מכה נפש בהמה ישלמנה. ומנסך את היין, ליכא למימר שניסכו ביין נסך שזרק בו, דלא קמחסריה ולא מידי, דהא מזבין ליה בר מדמי יין נסך שבו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:5.english: And one who pours a libation - [Pouring] wine for idol worship. And in Tractate Gittin (52b) it explains why he does not receive the greater punishment [so as to be exempt from payment]. [The categories of] one who defiles [food], one who mixes [terumah into non-sacred produce], and one who pours a libation are not written explicitly [in the Torah], and even so they are primary categories [of damage], because they are included in [the general category of] damage, and monetary damage is written in the Torah (Leviticus 24:18): "One who smites an animal's soul shall pay for it." And [as for] "one who pours a libation with the wine," it cannot be said that he rendered it forbidden as libation wine through libation wine that he threw into it, for [then] he did not cause him any loss at all, for behold, [the owner] can sell it [to a gentile] minus the value of the libation wine that is in it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:6.hebrew: ומטמא - שמגיע שרץ בתרומת כהן, דאפסדה מיניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:13:6.english: And one who renders ritually impure - Where he touches a creeping creature to a priest's teruma, for he caused him to lose it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:15:1.hebrew: גנב - המודה מעצמו וגזלן, דלא משלמי אלא קרן, ליתני:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:15:1.english: A thief - [One] who admits of his own accord, and a robber, who pay only the principal, let [Rabbi Oshaya] teach [them].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:15:2.hebrew: תנא ליה שומר חנם והשואל - דהתם נמי שייך גניבה, כגון שטען שנגנב הימנו והרי היא בידו, ואמרינן בפרק מרובה (לקמן בבא קמא דף סג:) דטוען טענת גנב כגנב, וטוען טענת גזלן כגזלן. והא דנקט הכא והשואל לאו דוקא, דהא לא משכחת ביה דנפטר, לא בטוען טענת גנב ולא בטוען טענת גזלן, שהרי הוא חייב בכולו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:15:2.english: He taught the unpaid bailee and the borrower - For there too [the law of] theft applies, such as where he claimed that it was stolen from him, and behold, it is in his possession; and we say in the chapter [entitled] "Merubah" (below, Bava Kamma 63b) that one who makes a claim of theft [is liable] like a thief, and one who makes a claim of robbery [is liable] like a robber. And that which [the Gemara] mentions here, "and the borrower," is not exact, for you cannot find regarding him [a case where] he is exempt, neither by making a claim of theft nor by making a claim of robbery, as he is liable for all [such losses].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:16:1.hebrew: דאתא לידיה בהיתירא - שומר חנם, אע"ג דהשתא טוען טענת גנב שנגנב הימנו, מיהו מעיקרא, כי אתא לידיה, בהיתירא אתא לידיה, וגנב וגזלן, ממונא אתא לידיה באיסורא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:16:1.english: That came into his possession in a permitted manner - [Regarding] an unpaid bailee, even though now he makes the claim of a thief, [namely,] that it was stolen from him, nevertheless initially, when it came into his possession, it came into his possession in a permitted manner, whereas [with] a thief and a robber, the property came into his possession in a prohibited manner.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:1:1.hebrew: ה"נ תני אדם שמירת גופו עליו - והאי דקתני ושמירתן עליך, אשארא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:1:1.english: Here too, teach: Man, the safeguarding of his body is upon him - And that which [the mishna] teaches, "and their safeguarding is upon you," [refers] to the rest [of the categories].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:1.hebrew: אימא מבעה זה המים - שאם שופך אדם מימיו לרה"ר, ובא אחר ונטנפו כליו, חייב השופכן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:1.english: Say that maveh is water - That if a person pours his water into the public domain, and another comes and his garments are soiled, the one who poured them is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:2.hebrew: כקדוח אש המסים - כמו שהאש שורף דבר הנימס, כגון זפת ושעוה וכל מיני רבב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:2.english: As fire kindles melting things - Just as fire burns something that melts, such as pitch, wax, and all kinds of grease.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:3.hebrew: מים תבעה אש - וכמים שמבעבעים את האש: כשנותנין מים על האש, נעשים כמין אבעבועות הרתיחות. וסיפא דקרא הכי הוא: "להודיע שמך לצריך" — כן תודיע שמך לצריך, כשתאבדם מן העולם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:3.english: Water boils fire - And like water that causes the fire to bubble: when one puts water on the fire, a kind of bubbles of boiling are formed. And the end of the verse is as follows: "To make Your name known to Your adversaries" — so may You make Your name known to Your adversaries when You destroy them from the world.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:4.hebrew: מי כתיב מים נבעו - לשון רבים, דליהוי משמע דמבעה אמים קאי, שהן מבעבעין את האש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:4.english: Is it written: "Water bubbled"? - [Which would be] a plural form, so that it would mean that "mabeh" refers to water, in that they cause the fire to bubble.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:5.hebrew: תבעה אש כתיב - דמשמע שהאש מבעבע המים, דתבעה לשון יחיד ולשון נקבה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:2:5.english: "Fire boils" is written - Which means that the fire boils the water, for tiveh is a singular and feminine form.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:3:1.english: [The mishna] is explaining - [Namely, that] "the maveh" is the fire.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:4:1.hebrew: דאית ביה תרתי - שן ורגל, וקרן לא קחשיב, דבתמין לא קמיירי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:4:1.english: In which there are two - Tooth and Foot, and [the tanna] does not count Horn, for [the mishna] does not deal with innocuous [animals].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:4:2.hebrew: מאי לא זה וזה - דקתני מתני' אשור ומבעה, לא זה וזה שיש בהן רוח חיים, ואי מבעה היינו אש, מי אית בו רוח חיים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:4:2.english: What is [the meaning of] "neither this nor that" - For the mishna teaches regarding ox and maveh: "Neither this one nor that one, in which there is a living spirit," and if maveh is fire, is there a living spirit in it?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:5:1.english: Primary categories - [The tanna] calls "primary categories" those that are written in Scripture.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:5:2.hebrew: שומר חנם - חייב בפשיעה, והשואל חייב אפילו באונסין, ושוכר ונושא שכר חייבים בגניבה ואבידה, וכ"ש בפשיעה. וכולהו כתיבי, כדתני בפרק השואל בבבא מציעא (דף צד:): פרשה ראשונה נאמרה בשומר חנם, שניה בשומר שכר, שלישית בשואל. הלכך אבות נינהו, ולקמן בעי מאי נינהו תולדות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:5:2.english: An unpaid bailee - [He] is liable for negligence, and the borrower is liable even for unavoidable accidents, and a renter and a paid bailee are liable for theft and loss, and all the more so for negligence. And all of them are written [in Scripture], as it is taught in chapter HaSho'el in Bava Metzia (94b): "The first section was stated regarding an unpaid bailee, the second regarding a paid bailee, [and] the third regarding a borrower." Therefore, they are primary categories, and further on [the Gemara] asks what the secondary categories are.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:5:3.english: Damage - One who injures his fellow gives him what he is worth now less than at first.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:5:4.hebrew: צער - אומדין כמה אדם העומד ידו ליקצץ ע"י חרב רוצה ליתן כדי שיתקצץ לו ע"י סם, דלית ליה צער כולי האי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:5:4.english: Pain - We assess how much a person whose hand is destined to be severed by a sword would be willing to give so that it will be severed for him by means of a drug, for he does not have that much pain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:5:5.hebrew: וריפוי ושבת ובושת - כולהו יליף מקראי בפרק החובל (לקמן בבא קמא דף פה.), וכיון דכתיבי, אבות נינהו. כל הנך דר' אושעיא הוא עצמו מזיק, דהנך ד' שומרים הן עצמם הזיקו, הואיל ולא שמרו כראוי, ובנזקין דאזיק גופו לא קמיירי מתני':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:5:5.english: And medical costs, and loss of livelihood, and humiliation - [The Gemara] derives all of them from verses in chapter HaChovel (below, Bava Kamma 85a), and since they are written [in Scripture], they are primary categories. All of these [categories] of Rabbi Oshaya are [cases where] he himself causes damage, for these four bailees, they themselves caused the damage since they did not safeguard properly; and with damages that [one's own] body caused, our mishna does not deal.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:6:1.hebrew: אלא לרב - דאמר מבעה זה אדם, הואיל ומיירי תנא דמתני', ליתני הני:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:6:1.english: But according to Rav - Who says that maveh is man, since the tanna of our mishna deals [with damage caused by man], let him teach these [categories as well].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:6:2.english: [The tanna] taught: Man - [This refers to] the Maveh of our mishna.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:7:1.hebrew: תנא אדם דאזיק שור - כלומר, נזקי ממון, דהא מבעה דומיא דבור קתני, ובור לא מיירי בנזקי אדם, דרחמנא פטריה לגמרי, כדתניא לקמן (בבא קמא דף נג:): שור ולא אדם, חמור ולא כלים. ואדם דאזיק שור, היכא כתיב דקרי ליה אב? דכתיב: ומכה נפש בהמה ישלמנה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:7:1.english: [The tanna] taught: A person who damaged an ox - That is to say, damage to property, for [the mishna] teaches maveh similar to pit, and pit does not deal with damage to a person, as the Merciful One completely exempted [it], as it is taught further on (Bava Kamma 53b): "An ox," and not a person; "a donkey," and not vessels. And [as for] a person who damaged an ox, where is it written that [the tanna] calls it a primary category? As it is written: "And one who strikes the life of an animal shall pay for it" [Leviticus 24:18].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:9:1.hebrew: בשלמא אדם דאזיק שור כו' - וכיון דלא דמי חיובינהו להדדי, תני להו בתרתי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:9:1.english: Granted, a person who damages an ox, etc. - And since their liabilities are not similar to each other, [Rabbi Oshaya] taught them as two [categories].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:9:2.hebrew: אדם דאזיק אדם - כגון ה' דברים דחובל בחבירו, ולקמיה פריך: הא ד' שומרין דר' אושעיא, אדם דאזיק שור הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 4b:9:2.english: A man who damages a man - Such as the five items of one who injures his fellow, and later [the Gemara] asks: But aren't the four bailees of Rabbi Oshaya [a case of] a man who damages an ox?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:12:1.hebrew: ועדים זוממין - פירש ריב"א, דאפילו שילם על פי העדים, זוממין חייבין, דלא שייך בממון כאשר זמם ולא כאשר עשה, דאפשר בחזרה. ור"י מפרש, דלא צריך להאי טעמא, דגבי ממון מחייבינן להו בק"ו, דגבי ממון עונשין מן הדין. והא דאמרינן במכות (דף ה:): הרגו אין נהרגים, היינו משום דהתם אין עונשין מן הדין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:12:1.english: And conspiring witnesses - The Riva explained that even if [the defendant] paid based on [the testimony of] the witnesses, the conspiring witnesses are liable, for "as he conspired, and not as he did" does not apply to monetary matters, since return [of the money] is possible. And the Ri explains that this reason is not necessary, for regarding monetary matters, we hold them liable through an a fortiori deduction (kal va-chomer), as regarding monetary matters, we penalize based on logical deduction (onshin min ha-din). And that which we say in Makkot (5b): "[If] they killed [him], they are not killed" — that is because there, we do not penalize based on logical deduction.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:13:1.hebrew: מנסך - פליגי בה בהנזקין (גיטין נב: ושם): חד אמר מנסך ממש, וחד אמר מערב:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:13:1.english: One who pours a libation - They disagree about it in [the chapter of] HaNizakin (Gittin 52b, and there): One says [it means] actually pouring a libation, and one says [it means] mixing [it with libation wine].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:2:1.hebrew: ואימא מבעה זה המים - פי': כיון דקרא לא דייקי, לא כמר ולא כמר. וא"ת: והיכן כתיב מים בתורה? וי"ל: מושלח, וכן הוא אומר (איוב ה׳:י׳): ושולח מים על פני חוצות. ואע"ג דשילח בעירה בבהמה איירי, מ"מ מים נמי משתמעי מיניה, מדאפקיה רחמנא בהמה בלשון ושלח. ולעיל דבעי: במאי מוקמינן לה? לא מצי מוקמינן במים, דכי נמי מוקמת במים, אית לן לאוקומי במילי דשור, מדכתיב בעירה. וא"ת: והני מים ה"ד? אי דמשקיל עליה בדקא דמיא, ובכח ראשון — כחו הוא; ואי בכח שני — גרמא בעלמא הוא, כדאמרינן בהנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עז:)! וי"ל: דמיירי בכח שני, וקמ"ל דבכח שני נמי חייב. א"נ: בתר דנחו; ולא דמי לבור, כגון פותקין ביבותיהן דלקמן (בבא קמא דף ל.)? ואע"ג דאתי במה הצד, הוה אמינא דאיצטריך לכותבו לחייב כלים, דמבור לא הוה שמעינן. והוה מצי למיפרך: מאי לא זה וזה שיש בהן רוח חיים? אלא דבלאו הכי משני שפיר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:2:1.english: And say [that] mav'eh is water - Explanation: Since the verses are not definitive, neither according to this Master nor according to that Master. And if you say: And where is water written in the Torah? And one can say: From "and he sends forth" (ve-shillach); and so it says (Job 5:10): "and sends water upon the fields." And even though "he sends forth his beast" deals with an animal, nevertheless, water is also implied by it, since the Merciful One expressed [damage by] an animal with the wording "and he sends forth" (ve-shillach). And above, when it asked: "To what do we establish it?", we could not establish it as water, because even if you would establish it as water, we must establish it in matters of an ox, since it is written "be'iroh" (his beast). And if you say: And this water, what are the circumstances? If [one] directed a rush of water upon it: if [it damages] by the first force, it is his [direct] force; and if by the second force, it is mere indirect causation (gerama), as we say in [perek] HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 77b)! And one can say: It is dealing with the second force, and it teaches us that by the second force as well one is liable. Alternatively: After it came to rest. And [if you say:] does it not resemble a pit, such as [the case of] those who open their drains below (Bava Kamma 30a)? And [one can say that] even though it could be derived via a common denominator (mah hatzad), one would have thought that it was necessary to write it to obligate for utensils, which we would not have learned from pit. And [the Gemara] could have objected: What [of that which the Mishnah states]: "not this one and that one, in which there is a living spirit"? Rather, [even] without that, it answered well.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:2:2.hebrew: מי כתיב מים נבעו - וא"ת: כי כתיב נמי נבעו, לא מיתוקמא מתניתי' במים, דמי קתני נבעה, כדדייק לעיל (בבא קמא דף ג:) גבי שן? וי"ל: דלא שייך לאקשויי אלא גבי שן, דליתני נבעה, שהשן עצמו נבעה, דמבעה משמע מגלה [דבר אחר שהיה מכוסה]; אבל במים שייך שפיר לישנא דמבעה, שהמים רותחים קרויים מבעבעים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:2:2.english: Is it written: "Water boiled"? - And if you say: Even if it were also written "niv'u", the Mishnah could [still] not be established as [referring to] water, for does [the Mishnah] teach "niv'ah", as [the Gemara] deduced above (Bava Kamma 3b) regarding tooth? And one can say: It is only relevant to object regarding tooth that it should teach "niv'ah", because the tooth itself is revealed, whereas "mav'eh" implies revealing [something else that was covered]; but regarding water, the phrasing "mav'eh" is well suited, for boiling water is called bubbling (meva'be'im).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:5:1.hebrew: שלשה עשר אבות נזיקין - ודיניהם י"ב, דשוכר כשומר שכר הוי או כשומר חנם הוי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:5:1.english: Thirteen primary categories of damage - And their laws are twelve, since a renter is [either] like a paid bailee or like an unpaid bailee.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:5:2.hebrew: שומר חנם והשואל - שומר חנם פטור מן הכל חוץ מן הפשיעה; שואל חייב בכל חוץ ממתה מחמת מלאכה; ונושא שכר חייב במקצת, בגניבה ואבידה, ופטור באונסין. לכך נקט להו בזה הסדר, ולא כסדר שנכתב בפרשה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:5:2.english: An unpaid bailee and the borrower - An unpaid bailee is exempt from everything except negligence; a borrower is liable for everything except when [the animal] dies on account of work; and a paid bailee is liable for part — for theft and loss — and is exempt from unavoidable accidents. Therefore, he taught them in this order, and not according to the order written in the Torah portion.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:7:1.hebrew: תרי גווני אדם - וא"ת: כיון דתני תרי גווני אדם, ליתני נמי ג' אבות בשור: הקרן, והשן, והרגל? וי"ל: דניחא ליה לכלול כולם בשור, כמו תנא דמתני':
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 4b:7:1.english: Two types of man - And if you say: Since he teaches two types of man, let him also teach three primary categories in [the category of] ox: horn (keren), tooth (shen), and foot (regel)? And one can say: It was preferable for him to include all of them in "ox," like the Tanna of our Mishnah.
